provenance.scope: Authored content potential only. This audit does not assert that a node is currently known, available, cast, active, or applied in any live game state. Those runtime states must be joined from live simulation data.
provenance.method: Direct authored-field projection. effectMode derives only from technique via visualMapping.effectModeByTechnique. visualArchetype and anchorClass use documented precedence over authored primitive and target fields. Names and glosses are not interpreted.

effects.gloss: Enumerate the doorways that used to be there. A threshold that has been closed leaves a shape in the wall even after the door itself is gone.

Locate exactly where a standing gate could be erased, and measure exactly how far a step through it would once have carried. Nothing else in the grid maps a threshold's removal this precisely before it happens.
What the ward used to protect becomes visible again, once — the last thing a sealed gate reveals before whatever comes next removes even the memory of standing there.
Locate two thresholds' worth of memory in the wall precisely enough that erasing them becomes simple bookkeeping for whoever a sapper hands the working to.
A mage who already holds enough of this cell's craft can tell, from a hole in the wall alone, whether a gate could have been opened there at all.
Hold the seam itself long enough that its ward becomes as legible as everything on either side of it — and from there, exactly how far a step through would carry.
Find the door that isn't there anymore by the way the wall still remembers its shape. Nothing needs to open for a whole place's worth of closed thresholds to become legible at once.
A tally of every silence in a lecture hall — legible only once you already know which minds in it are actually listening. From there, the hall's true teaching speed is obvious.
Once a mind's refusals are catalogued in full, forcing an answer out of it stops requiring its cooperation.
A scholar who already knows enough of her own mentem practice can drill a sealed mind's blind spots on command — but only with that much of the craft in hand.
Learn a mind well enough to know exactly which subject it steers around. What is being protected is now marked for whoever is unmaking it.
Notice what a mind has gone quiet about. What a scholar refuses to think about is where the hole will be cut, and now that place is marked.
The last secret a mind can keep, found and marked in the same instant. Nothing else in the grid opens a hole this precisely.
Once a mind is known this precisely, exactly how much could still be taught from it becomes obvious too — for whatever good that does the mind that has been opened.
Mark exactly where an entry could be struck from the ledger without its absence ever reading as a gap — the striking itself is a different working.
A forger who already knows this cell's whole catalogue can rewrite an entry fast enough that nobody checks the date.
Learn a name well enough to know exactly which syllable, mispronounced, makes it stop working. The gap between the true name and the near-miss is where a stolen copy hides.
Read not one name but the whole shelf at once — audible only once the catalogue's own rhythm is already legible to you.
Notice a name by the shape of its absence — the gap left in a conversation that is carefully never naming something.
Mark a name for both copying and erasure in the same working. Nothing else in the grid locates a removal this precisely while marking the copy in the same breath.
Once a name is unwritten, exactly how well anything built to conceal it will work finally becomes legible — the concealment itself is an older, separate working.
The full map of where this ground will give way, cross-referenced against exactly how fast the surface above it could still be built. Nothing else in the grid predicts a collapse this precisely.
What collapses also releases whatever the hollow was hiding — a last yield, once, from ground that will not give again.
Notice which page of the hillside is already hollow, or wants to be. Where a foundation cannot be set is where a floor most easily gives way.
Set a price on a vein before the first pick strikes it — audible only once the seam's yield is already known to someone in the room.
Tables cross-indexing every seam ever found against what it actually paid out. From here, the yield of any vein anywhere in the world is a lookup, not a guess.
Once the fault lines of a place are already mapped, the same tables say how fast a wall could stand there.
Read a hollow down to what is structurally still there. What is left standing after that is exactly what a sapper's crew can be told to finish.
A surveyor who already knows enough of this ground can price the salvage from a hollowing before the digging even starts.
The seam between a threshold and the earth it stands in stops holding, and the ground either side of it goes with it.
The caster passes a threshold that never registers her passing, because the threshold has quietly forgotten it has an inside and an outside.
The ground on both sides of the threshold stays wrong indefinitely, and the wrongness widens the longer it is left.
Whatever tries to cross where the threshold used to be is struck by the absence of a place to stand.
Once the scale of the hollow is understood, no builder in the universe trusts ground this practiced at swallowing thresholds, and construction everywhere slows a little for it.
Once the threshold's hold on its structure is understood, severing it drops whatever it was bearing all at once.
The ground around the severed hold keeps refusing to bear weight for as long as the understanding of it lasts.
A place stops being a place that can be crossed, arrived at, or opened onto, permanently and everywhere within the working's reach.
Once what is being shut is truly understood, whatever still tries to stand at the threshold is struck by the fact that there is no longer a threshold there to stand at.
Once the working itself has been perceived, the erasure lands twice as clean, its own trace gone with the rest.
A mind this practiced at unmaking finds new derivations slower; the same hole that empties a victim's head thins its owner's.
The caster's own passage through a room stops registering as a memory in anyone who witnessed it.
The caster's own teaching thins, in the same coin she spends elsewhere: a hole where a lesson used to land cleanly.
There is no impact transient, no struck note — only a sine that was there, and then a silence exactly the shape it left.
The working refuses even its own caster an account of itself; nothing about how it was done can afterward be derived from having done it.
The name will not form in any mouth that tries it, not even a hostile one that already half-knows the sound.
There is no longer a name for anything that would need answering to; the question of who this is stops being a question with an answer.
Once the scale of the unnaming is understood, nobody can be taught to call the caster by anything at all, and teaching that depends on the name fails outright.
Once a mind's sealing is properly understood, the seal itself becomes near-total: nothing that could name the caster still can.
A mind sealed this completely against being read from outside finds it harder to read anything new from outside either.
One spoken claim is struck out of whoever repeats it, mid-sentence, without touching anything else they know.
The caster becomes, functionally, un-attributable: nothing that could trace this working back to her can.
A mage this deep into the sealed-mind track finds the silence bites back on its own, striking anything that tries to force the name loose.
Once the flaw is noticed for what it is, every shipment behind it is quietly suspect, and the universe's stone is worth less across the board.
The wall built on the flawed course fails exactly where the flaw was left, on a day nobody chose.
A permanent thinness enters the universe's supply of good stone: it is still there, and none of it is good anymore.
Once a civilization has enough Perdo Terram in its hands to know what it is doing, its own construction slows: the habit of taking too much does not stay confined to enemy walls.
The ground does not merely refuse to hold weight; it keeps refusing, indefinitely, in a widening circle.
Once the hollow is understood for what it is, whatever falls into it falls further than the drop should allow.
The universe's construction slows permanently and on purpose: nothing further is asked of the ground, ever again.
What is struck is not weakened. It is un-quarried, taken back past the point of ever having been stone that could be set.
A floor under how much ground stays unusable once the hollow is opened.
Opening a hollow costs some of the mage's own defensive resolve; it never rises past this while the hollow stands.
A cap on how much a tested frame is reinforced in the testing: the point is information, not strength.
A gate on a gate: the crossing is guaranteed to hold this reliably, and guaranteed never to be pushed past this — the hollow ground on the far side is the whole design, not an accident of power.
A floor under how much of the arrival ground stays unusable to whoever is waiting there.
Once the seam is legible, the hollow ground it opens holds at least this much unusable space.
The same understanding that opens the hollow further caps how well the mage can also defend herself while doing it.
A floor under a mage's own guardedness: it never slips below this, whatever the provocation.
A whole college's devotion floors out higher than any two minds could manage alone.
A faculty that shares attention also shares its questions, and never falls below this pace of answering them.
Once a thief's reach into this mind is legible, at least this much of what they came for turns around on them.
Using a mind as bait costs some of its total secrecy, once the trap has been seen for what it is.
As total a secrecy floor as the grid permits, bought by a ceiling that forbids ever pushing it higher: the doctrine is complete, and complete is all it will ever be.
A firmer floor than plain stillness: the sealed mind holds its secrecy under real pressure.
A mind trained to seal itself cannot be rushed past this pace, however devoted the teacher.
A floor under how fast a faculty can study a subject once it has a name to hold the study by.

A floor of twenty years held against a life's own decline — modest, and the only one of the three life-extension effects that asks nothing of Intellego to trigger, only enough of it already studied to have earned the working.
A floor under how reliably the named thing arrives, whatever grounds it might otherwise have claimed.
Once it is understood how a held name decays, refusing that decay is worth a century, guaranteed — but only once the decay itself has been made legible to refuse.

Two hundred years guaranteed against decline, and a hard cap at four hundred: the working extends a life, it does not abolish the idea of one, and it can never exceed what a mage's own species base permits.
A faculty led by a mage who has outlasted her own decline studies no slower than this, for as long as she is there to lead it.
Once a shared registry of names is legible to the whole faculty, study of them never falls below this pace.
The same open ledger, once understood, also steadies how fast a name's holder can be taught to use it.
A hard cap on this refusal's own yield: the point is what is left in the ground, not what comes out of it.
A hard cap on what this one quarry will ever give up again, deliberately imposed.
The floor under a construction effort large enough to never fully complete.
The quarries feeding an endless course never drop below this, or the course stops, and it may not stop.
Once the doctrine's discipline is legible, a seam left unopened recovers its yield no slower than this. The fallow ground pays, eventually, for having been left alone.
Fallow ground defends itself, once that is understood — but only up to a cap, since nothing has been raised to reinforce it further.
Land that has never been cut defends itself more reliably than any built wall, and no better than this — the doctrine does not build, it only holds.
